# --cache chooses the build cache, and with --clean deletes it, leaving
# projects' outputs and state in place.
env BIT_CACHE=disk://$WORK/cache
cd repo
exec git init -q
exec git add .
exec git -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=Test commit -qm base
exec git worktree add -q ../wt
exec git worktree add -q ../other
bit
exists $WORK/cache/actions

# A worktree using another cache misses.
cd $WORK/other
bit --cache disk://$WORK/elsewhere --plan
stdout '^lib \+ '
bit --cache disk://$WORK/elsewhere
stdout '^lib ▶ '
exists $WORK/elsewhere/actions

bit --cache $BIT_CACHE --clean
! stdout .
! exists $WORK/cache/actions
! exists $WORK/cache/cas
exists $WORK/elsewhere/actions
exists $WORK/repo/lib.txt

# The project that built is still up to date.
cd $WORK/repo
bit
stdout '^lib · no changes$'

# Another worktree now runs the command instead of restoring.
cd $WORK/wt
bit --plan
stdout '^lib \+ '
bit
stdout '^lib ▶ '
grep '\Arun\nrun\nrun\n\z' $WORK/lib.log

-- repo/.gitignore --
lib.txt
-- repo/BUILD.bit --
lib = exec {
  command = "echo run >> ../lib.log; echo lib > lib.txt"
  outputs = "lib.txt"
}
